equation_request.abstract: We investigate quantum computational complexity of calculating partition functions of Ising models. We construct a quantum algorithm for an additive approximation of Ising partition functions on square lattices. To this end, we utilize the overlap mapping developed by Van den Nest, Dür, and Briegel [Phys. Rev. Lett. 98, 117207 (2007)] and its interpretation through measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC). We specify an algorithmic domain, on which the proposed algorithm works, and an approximation scale, which determines the accuracy of the approximation. We show that the proposed algorithm does a nontrivial task, which would be intractable on any classical computer, by showing the problem solvable by the proposed quantum algorithm are BQP-complete. In the construction of the BQP-complete problem coupling strengths and magnetic fields take complex values. However, the Ising models that are of central interest in statistical physics and computer science consist of real coupling strengths and magnetic fields. Thus we extend the algorithmic domain of the proposed algorithm to such a real physical parameter region and calculate the approximation scale explicitly. We found that the overlap mapping and its MBQC interpretation improves the approximation scale exponentially compared to a straightforward constant depth quantum algorithm. On the other hand, the proposed quantum algorithm also provides us a partial evidence that there exist no efficient classical algorithm for a multiplicative approximation of the Ising partition functions even on the square lattice. This result supports that the proposed quantum algorithm does a nontrivial task also in the physical parameter region.

specification.problem: Additive approximation of the Ising partition function Z = sum_s exp(sum J_ij s_i s_j + sum h_i s_i) on a square lattice, via the overlap mapping (Van den Nest, Dür, Briegel) and its MBQC interpretation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: the standard overlap-mapping identity expressing Z as an inner product between a product state and a graph (cluster) state on a tiny 2x2 square lattice, plus the Hadamard-test style estimation of that overlap. Out of scope: the specific algorithmic domain, the approximation scale, the BQP-completeness proof, the extension to real parameters and the explicit scale calculation, the exponential improvement over constant-depth algorithms, and the hardness of multiplicative approximation.

symbols.domain: complex in general (abstract); real in the physical region
complex in general; real in the physical region

symbols.meaning: product state encoding J and h

equations.label: Ising partition function
equations.description: Partition function with the inverse temperature absorbed into J and h.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the Ising partition function; the abstract states only that Z is the quantity to be approximated.
assumptions: Inverse temperature absorbed into J and h

equations.label: Graph state
equations.description: Graph state on the lattice used in the overlap mapping.
equations.justification: Standard definition of graph states; the abstract mentions the overlap mapping and MBQC but gives no formulas.
assumptions: The graph state is built on the lattice or a related graph

equations.label: Overlap form of Z
equations.description: Z is proportional to the overlap of a product state with a graph state. The exact single-qubit states and the constant c are not reconstructed here.
equations.abstract_quote: we utilize the overlap mapping developed by Van den Nest, Dür, and Briegel
equations.justification: The overlap mapping is named in the abstract, which implies that Z is an overlap between states. The detailed form is from background knowledge of that work and is not verified; the lattice used for the graph state may differ from the Ising lattice.
assumptions: Details of |\alpha_i\rangle and c are left unspecified

equations.label: Hadamard-test estimate
equations.description: Generic way to estimate the real and imaginary parts of an overlap with additive error. This is not claimed to be the paper's MBQC-based procedure.
equations.justification: Generic overlap-estimation primitive, used as a placeholder because the abstract does not give the actual algorithm.
assumptions: The overlap is expressed as an amplitude of a unitary circuit

registers.name: spin/qubit register
registers.role: One qubit per lattice site, holding the graph state or MBQC resource state

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle_{anc}|+\rangle^{\otimes n}, assumed for the graph-state preparation

steps.description: Define the instance (2x2 lattice with chosen J_ij, h_i) and write Z as in eq_1.
Map Z to the overlap of a product state with a graph state.
Estimate the overlap with additive error, either through the MBQC interpretation or, as a stand-in, a Hadamard test.

specification.measurement: Ancilla measured in the Z basis for the Hadamard test, a generic assumption; the paper's MBQC measurement pattern is not specified in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Rescale the estimated overlap by the constant c to give an additive approximation of Z. The error scale is not specified.
assumptions: No scope was given, so a tiny 2x2 lattice instance was chosen.
The overlap mapping details are recalled from background and not verified.
The Hadamard test replaces the paper's MBQC-based procedure as a placeholder.
